newsitem.title: UK: Paper Brent, Dated higher on lower Nov loadings.
newsitem.headline: Paper Brent, Dated higher on lower Nov loadings.

text.p: Prompt paper North Sea Brent spreads widened again on Wednesday afternoon as buyers jockeyed for position following the announcement of a lower-than-expected November loading programme.
Nov/Dec Brent traded to +56 cents from +40 cents on Tuesday and offers backed away to +58 cents.
Dated Brent also moved higher with an end-Oct cargo offered at Nov +5 cents after trades on Tuesday at Nov -5 and -8 cents.
"The market was a little taken aback by the lower Brent programme because there was no real reason to suspect it," said a trader.

Brent will load the equivalent of 42.2 cargoes in November compared to 46.9 in October. But overall North Sea volumes are set to rise in November to 4.62 million barrels per day from 4.4 million bpd in October, mainly because of the expected return of maintenance of the Gullfaks field.
But some other North Sea values appeared slightly lower in a trade for Oseberg at Dated Brent +47 cents.

Offshore loading Norwegian grades with fixed shipping rates, however, were helped by fast rising rates on the spot chartering market. Statfjord for November sold at +60 cents on Tuesday, dealers said.

In the Mediterranean, the sour crude market was firm, although most traders said that a Urals deal reported on Tuesday at the equivalent of Dated Brent -52.5 cents cif Augusta was above market levels.
"They bought it fob and tried to say it was equal to a very high cif number," said one trader.
The cargo was resold into Greece on a quotes-related basis, traders said.
Traders said the market was still fairly tight with some gaps in the late October loading programme at Novorossiisk because of berthing delays in recent days due to bad weather.
